title: Adaptive Momentum and Nonlinear Damping for Neural Network Training
claim: Our adaptive-damping optimizers close most of the gap between simple momentum SGD and Adam on Transformer training, without per-parameter learning rates.
layout: 2 line-plot panels side by side, shared legend below, double-headed 'Gap' arrows
description: Two side-by-side line plots of training loss. The left panel is titled DistilBERT (SST-2), with epochs on the x-axis. The right panel is titled GPT2-XS (OpenWebText), with steps on the x-axis. A shared 'Loss' label sits on the y-axis. Four colored curves appear in each panel: Adam in red, mSGD in purple, CD (Ours) in green, and iKFAD (Ours) in blue. In both panels the purple mSGD curve sits well above the others. The red, green and blue curves fall to lower loss. In the left panel the green and blue curves finish below Adam. In the right panel the three curves nearly overlap at the end. Bold 'Gap' labels with black double-headed arrows mark the distance between mSGD and the other curves. A boxed legend runs along the bottom. The eye goes first to the purple curve and the gap arrows.
caption: Adam-mSGD gap: Selected experiments demonstrating that CD and iKFAD can reduce the gap between Adam and mSGD without per-parameter adaptive learning rates on language modeling tasks using Transformers.
abstract: Momentum Stochastic Gradient Descent (mSGD) relies on a fixed momentum coefficient shared across all parameters, failing to account for the heterogeneous structure of modern loss landscapes. In this work, we adopt a continuous-time formulation to introduce individual, adaptive momentum coefficients regulated by the kinetic energy of each model parameter. This mechanism automatically adjusts to evolving training dynamics to maintain stability without sacrificing convergence speed. We demonstrate that this adaptive friction is inextricably linked to cubic damping, a suppression mechanism from structural dynamics. We additionally introduce two optimization schemes by augmenting the continuous dynamics of mSGD and Adam with a cubic damping term. Empirically, our methods demonstrate robustness and match or outperform Adam on training ViT, BERT, and GPT2 tasks where mSGD typically struggles. We further provide theoretical results establishing the exponential convergence of the proposed schemes.
